title: Oral direct thrombin inhibitors or oral factor Xa inhibitors versus conventional anticoagulants for the treatment of pulmonary embolism.
research_query: What is the comparative efficacy and safety of oral direct thrombin inhibitors (DTIs) or oral factor Xa inhibitors versus conventional anticoagulants for the long-term treatment of pulmonary embolism?
overall_conclusion: There is probably little or no difference between DOACs and conventional anticoagulation in the prevention of recurrent PE, recurrent VTE, DVT, all-cause mortality, and major bleeding, with moderate or low certainty of evidence.

key_points.statement: Available evidence shows there is probably little or no difference between DOACs and conventional anticoagulation in the prevention of recurrent PE, recurrent VTE, DVT, all-cause mortality, and major bleeding, with moderate or low certainty of evidence.

There was no clear difference in the efficacy and safety of oral direct thrombin inhibitors compared with conventional anticoagulation in preventing recurrent PE, recurrent VTE, DVT, and major bleeding.
There was no clear difference between oral factor Xa inhibitors and conventional anticoagulation in the prevention of recurrent PE, recurrent VTE, DVT, all-cause mortality, and major bleeding.
The certainty of evidence for oral factor Xa inhibitors was downgraded to moderate and low due to imprecision from a low number of events and inconsistency due to clinical heterogeneity.

title: Digital technology for early identification of exacerbations in people with cystic fibrosis.

title: Oral dextrose gel to prevent hypoglycaemia in at-risk neonates.
research_query: What is the effectiveness and safety of oral dextrose gel compared to placebo, no intervention, or other therapies in preventing neonatal hypoglycaemia in at-risk infants?
overall_conclusion: Oral dextrose gel reduces the risk of neonatal hypoglycaemia in at-risk infants and probably reduces the risk of major neurological disability at two years of age or greater without increasing the risk of adverse events compared to placebo gel.

key_points.statement: Oral dextrose gel reduces the risk of neonatal hypoglycaemia in at-risk infants and probably reduces the risk of major neurological disability at two years of age or greater without increasing the risk of adverse events compared to placebo gel.
Oral dextrose gel reduces the risk of hypoglycaemia compared to placebo.
Oral dextrose gel probably reduces the risk of receipt of treatment for hypoglycaemia during the initial hospital stay compared to placebo.
There is probably little or no difference in the risk of adverse events in infants who receive oral dextrose gel compared to placebo gel.
There are no studies comparing oral dextrose with comparators such as no treatment, standard care, or other therapies.

title: Selective oestrogen receptor modulators (SERMs) for endometriosis.
research_query: What is the effectiveness and safety of selective oestrogen receptor modulators (SERMs) compared to placebo, no treatment, other medical treatments, or surgery in the management of endometriosis?
overall_conclusion: Based on a single, small RCT and incomplete data, it is uncertain what the effects of SERMs are on pain relief in surgically treated patients with endometriosis.

key_points.statement: Based on a single, small RCT and incomplete data, it is uncertain what the effects of SERMs are on pain relief in surgically treated patients with endometriosis.

In women after surgical treatment, the time to return of pelvic pain (defined as two months of pain equal to or more severe than pain at study entry) was more rapid in the raloxifene group compared to placebo.
It is uncertain whether raloxifene improves the incidence of adverse events including pelvic pain, ovarian cyst, headache, migraine, and depression compared to placebo.
There was a statistically significant difference in mental health quality of life by 12 months in favour of placebo treatment compared to raloxifene.
Evidence regarding the effect of raloxifene on the biopsy-proven recurrence rate of endometriosis compared to placebo is of very low quality and remains uncertain.

title: Corticosteroids for periorbital and orbital cellulitis.
research_query: What is the effectiveness and safety of adjunctive corticosteroids compared to antibiotics alone in the treatment of periorbital and orbital cellulitis, considering outcomes such as length of hospital stay, duration of antibiotic use, visual acuity preservation, pain reduction, and need for surgical intervention?
overall_conclusion: There is insufficient evidence to draw conclusions about the use of corticosteroids in the treatment of periorbital and orbital cellulitis.

key_points.statement: There is insufficient evidence to draw conclusions about the use of corticosteroids in the treatment of periorbital and orbital cellulitis.

There was no observed difference between adjunctive corticosteroids and antibiotics alone regarding length of hospital stay, duration of antibiotics, preservation of visual acuity at 12 weeks, pain scores on day 3, or the need for surgical intervention.

No major complications of orbital cellulitis were seen in either the intervention or control group, and no side effects of corticosteroids were reported, although it is unclear which side effects were assessed.
The certainty of evidence for all outcomes was very low, downgraded for risk of bias and imprecision.

title: Surgery for idiopathic epiretinal membrane.
research_query: What are the effects of surgical removal of idiopathic epiretinal membrane compared to no intervention, placebo, or sham treatment, particularly in terms of visual acuity, quality of life, and adverse events?
overall_conclusion: For mild symptomatic epiretinal membrane, the value of surgery is uncertain, with low-certainty evidence suggesting that watchful waiting or deferred surgery may offer outcomes as favourable as immediate surgery.

key_points.statement: For mild symptomatic epiretinal membrane, the value of surgery is uncertain, with low-certainty evidence suggesting that watchful waiting or deferred surgery may offer outcomes as favourable as immediate surgery.
Low-certainty evidence indicates that at 12 months, visual acuity was higher in the immediate surgery group compared to the watchful waiting/deferred surgery group.
Evidence regarding the effect of immediate surgery on gains of 0.3 logMAR or more of visual acuity is very uncertain.

Low-certainty evidence shows that no serious adverse events occurred in either group at 12 months, although one participant developed chronic minimal cystoid macular oedema following immediate surgery.
The included study did not measure quality of life.

title: Interleukin-6 blocking agents for treating COVID-19: a living systematic review.
research_query: What is the efficacy and safety of interleukin-6 (IL-6) blocking agents, such as tocilizumab and sarilumab, compared to standard care or placebo in the treatment of COVID-19 across varying levels of disease severity?
overall_conclusion: Tocilizumab reduces all-cause mortality at D28 and probably results in slightly fewer serious adverse events than standard care alone or placebo, but probably results in little or no increase in clinical improvement at D28; evidence for the effect of sarilumab is uncertain and evidence for other anti-IL6 agents is unavailable.

key_points.statement: Tocilizumab reduces all-cause mortality at D28 and probably results in slightly fewer serious adverse events than standard care alone or placebo, but probably results in little or no increase in clinical improvement at D28, while evidence for the effect of sarilumab is uncertain and evidence for other anti-IL6 agents is unavailable.
Tocilizumab reduces all-cause mortality at D28 compared to standard care alone or placebo, based on high-certainty evidence.
Tocilizumab probably results in slightly fewer serious adverse events than standard care alone or placebo, based on moderate-certainty evidence.
Evidence is uncertain regarding the effect of sarilumab on all-cause mortality at D28, all-cause mortality at ≥ D60, and serious adverse events.
The effect of tocilizumab on the proportion of participants with a WHO Clinical Progression Score of level 7 or above at D28 is uncertain.

title: Antibiotic therapy versus no antibiotic therapy for children aged 2 to 59 months with WHO-defined non-severe pneumonia and wheeze.
research_query: What is the efficacy of antibiotic therapy compared to no antibiotic therapy in children aged 2 to 59 months with WHO-defined non-severe pneumonia and wheeze?
overall_conclusion: There is currently not enough evidence to support or challenge the continued use of antibiotics for the treatment of non-severe pneumonia in children aged 2 to 59 months with WHO-defined non-severe pneumonia and wheeze.

key_points.statement: There is currently not enough evidence to support or challenge the continued use of antibiotics for the treatment of non-severe pneumonia in children aged 2 to 59 months with WHO-defined non-severe pneumonia and wheeze.
Antibiotic therapy may result in a reduction of treatment failure, based on low-certainty evidence.
Antibiotic therapy probably results in little or no difference to clinical cure, based on moderate-certainty evidence.
Antibiotic therapy results in little or no difference to relapse, based on low-certainty evidence.
Antibiotic therapy results in little or no difference to treatment harms, based on low-certainty evidence.

title: Interventions for frostbite injuries.
research_query: What are the benefits and harms of different medical interventions, such as pharmacological therapy, topical treatments, or rewarming techniques, for managing frostbite injuries?
overall_conclusion: There is a paucity of evidence regarding interventions for frostbite injuries, though very low-quality evidence from one small trial indicates that iloprost, and iloprost plus rtPA, in combination with buflomedil may reduce the need for amputation in people with severe frostbite compared to buflomedil alone.

key_points.statement: There is a paucity of evidence regarding interventions for frostbite injuries, though very low-quality evidence from one small trial indicates that iloprost, and iloprost plus rtPA, in combination with buflomedil may reduce the need for amputation in people with severe frostbite compared to buflomedil alone.
Iloprost and iloprost plus rtPA may reduce the rate of amputations in people with severe frostbite compared to buflomedil alone, based on very low-quality evidence.
Iloprost may be as effective as iloprost plus rtPA at reducing the amputation rate in people with severe frostbite, based on very low-quality evidence.
Adverse events including flushing, nausea, palpitations, and vomiting were common, although evidence for these outcomes was of very low quality.
Outcomes regarding acute pain, chronic pain, ability to perform activities of daily living, quality of life, or occupational effects were not measured.

title: Visual cycle modulators versus placebo or observation for the prevention and treatment of geographic atrophy due to age-related macular degeneration.
research_query: What is the efficacy and safety of visual cycle modulators, such as emixustat and fenretinide, compared to placebo or observation for the prevention and treatment of geographic atrophy due to age-related macular degeneration?
overall_conclusion: There is limited evidence to support the use of visual cycle modulators (emixustat and fenretinide) for the treatment of established geographic atrophy due to AMD.

key_points.statement: There is limited evidence to support the use of visual cycle modulators (emixustat and fenretinide) for the treatment of established geographic atrophy due to AMD.

Emixustat may result in little or no difference compared to placebo in best-corrected visual acuity (BCVA) change, loss of 15 ETDRS letters or more of BCVA, and the annual growth rate of geographic atrophy, based on low-certainty evidence.
The onset of choroidal neovascularisation (CNV) may be reduced in those treated with fenretinide or emixustat compared to placebo, although the evidence was uncertain and of low certainty.
The most common adverse events for emixustat and fenretinide were ocular in nature, specifically delayed dark adaptation and chromatopsia, which were dose-dependent and resolved after drug cessation.
Included studies had a high risk of attrition bias, primarily due to the ocular adverse effects of emixustat and fenretinide.

title: Interventions to reduce body temperature to 35 ⁰C to 37 ⁰C in adults and children with traumatic brain injury.
research_query: What are the effects of pharmacological or physical interventions aimed at reducing body temperature to 35 °C to 37.5 °C in adults and children admitted to hospital after traumatic brain injury?
overall_conclusion: There is very low-certainty evidence regarding the effect of reducing body temperature to 35 °C to 37.5 °C in people with TBI, and further research is needed to increase certainty in this field.

key_points.statement: There is very low-certainty evidence regarding the effect of reducing body temperature to 35 °C to 37.5 °C in people with TBI, and further research is needed to increase certainty in this field.
It is uncertain whether intravenous paracetamol influenced mortality at 28 days in adult participants admitted to intensive care units.
The evidence for mortality following intravenous paracetamol is of very low certainty due to imprecision and a high risk of selective reporting bias.

Available evidence did not report on the primary outcome of poor outcome at the end of follow-up (death or dependency) or secondary outcomes including intracranial haemorrhage, extracranial haemorrhage, abnormal intracranial pressure, or pneumonia and other serious infections.

title: Targeted therapy for metastatic renal cell carcinoma.
research_query: What are the effects of targeted therapies, including TKI-based treatments and immune checkpoint inhibitors, on progression-free survival, overall survival, and adverse events in patients with clear cell metastatic renal cell carcinoma who are naïve to systemic therapy?
overall_conclusion: Based on low to high certainty of evidence, several combinations of immune checkpoint inhibitors appear to be superior to single-agent targeted therapy in terms of PFS and OS, and with a favourable AE profile, while some single-agent targeted therapies demonstrated similar or improved oncological outcomes compared to others.

key_points.statement: Based on low to high certainty of evidence, several combinations of immune checkpoint inhibitors appear to be superior to single-agent targeted therapy in terms of PFS and OS, and with a favourable AE profile, while some single-agent targeted therapies demonstrated similar or improved oncological outcomes compared to others.
Sunitinib probably reduces PFS as compared to avelumab plus axitinib and pembrolizumab plus axitinib, and reduces OS as compared to nivolumab plus ipilimumab.
Pazopanib may result in little to no difference in PFS, OS, and SAEs as compared to sunitinib.
Sunitinib probably increases SAEs as compared to nivolumab plus ipilimumab.
The certainty of evidence for the comparisons ranged from high to very low, and all comparisons were based on single trials.

title: Behavioural activation therapy for depression in adults with non-communicable diseases.
research_query: What are the effects of behavioural activation therapy compared to various control groups (e.g., no treatment, waiting list, other psychological therapy, pharmacological treatment, or treatment as usual) for the treatment of depression in adults with non-communicable diseases such as cardiovascular disease, diabetes, cancer, and chronic respiratory conditions?
overall_conclusion: Evidence from this review was not sufficient to draw conclusions on the efficacy and acceptability of behavioural activation for the treatment of depression in adults with NCDs.

key_points.statement: Evidence from this review was not sufficient to draw conclusions on the efficacy and acceptability of behavioural activation for the treatment of depression in adults with NCDs.

Treatment efficacy (remission) was greater for behavioural activation than for comparators in the short term (low-certainty evidence) and medium term (moderate-certainty evidence), though effects were reduced in the long term (moderate-certainty evidence).
There was no evidence of a difference in depression symptoms between behavioural activation and comparators in the short term (low-certainty evidence).
There was no evidence of a difference in treatment acceptability in the short term and medium term (low-certainty evidence).
Included studies were at risk of performance bias and potential conflict of interest arising from author involvement in the development of the intervention.

title: Blood transfusion for preventing primary and secondary stroke in people with sickle cell disease.
research_query: What are the risks and benefits of chronic blood transfusion regimens compared to alternative treatments, such as hydroxyurea and phlebotomy, for primary and secondary stroke prevention in individuals with sickle cell disease?
overall_conclusion: Long-term red cell transfusions reduce stroke risk in high-risk children without previous long-term transfusions, while switching to hydroxyurea with phlebotomy for primary and secondary prevention has little or no effect on liver iron concentration and increases the risk of sickle cell disease-related events in secondary prevention; other evidence is of very low quality.

key_points.statement: Long-term red cell transfusions reduce the risk of stroke in children at higher risk who have not had previous long-term transfusions, while switching to hydroxyurea with phlebotomy for primary and secondary prevention has little or no effect on liver iron concentration and increases the risk of sickle cell disease-related events in secondary prevention, though most other evidence is of very low quality.

Long-term red cell transfusions probably reduce the incidence of clinical stroke and may reduce the incidence of other sickle cell disease-related complications, such as acute chest syndrome, in children with no previous long-term transfusions.
Switching to hydroxyurea and phlebotomy may increase the risk of sickle cell disease-related serious adverse events in children and adolescents in secondary prevention.
Switching to hydroxyurea and phlebotomy may have little or no effect on liver iron concentrations in children in primary prevention.
The quality of evidence was very low to moderate across different outcomes due to high risk of bias from lack of blinding, indirectness, and imprecise outcome estimates.

title: GLP-1 receptor agonists for Parkinson's disease.
research_query: What is the effectiveness and safety of GLP-1 receptor agonists in improving motor impairment, health-related quality of life, and other outcomes for individuals with Parkinson's disease compared to conventional treatment, placebo, or no treatment?
overall_conclusion: Low- or very low-certainty evidence suggests that exenatide may improve motor impairment for people with PD, while its effectiveness for improving HRQoL, non-motor outcomes, ADLs, and psychological outcomes is unclear.

key_points.statement: Low- or very low-certainty evidence suggests that exenatide may improve motor impairment for people with PD, while its effectiveness for improving HRQoL, non-motor outcomes, ADLs, and psychological outcomes is unclear.

Low-certainty evidence suggests exenatide improves motor impairment as assessed by the MDS-UPDRS Part III in the off-medication state compared to placebo, and very low-certainty evidence suggests it improves the same measure compared to no treatment at 14 months.

Low-certainty evidence suggests that exenatide has little or no effect on health-related quality of life as assessed by the PDQ-39 Summary Index, EQ5D, or EQ5D visual analogue scale compared to placebo.

Serious adverse events were recorded in trials of exenatide, but they were considered unrelated to the intervention or there was very low-certainty evidence of little or no effect on the number of serious adverse events.
The evidence regarding the improvement of motor impairment, health-related quality of life, and weight loss is characterized as low or very low-certainty.

title: Standard versus biofilm antimicrobial susceptibility testing to guide antibiotic therapy in cystic fibrosis.
research_query: Does biofilm antimicrobial susceptibility testing improve microbiological and clinical outcomes compared to conventional antimicrobial susceptibility testing in the treatment of Pseudomonas aeruginosa pulmonary infections in people with cystic fibrosis?
overall_conclusion: Current evidence is insufficient to recommend choosing antibiotics based on biofilm antimicrobial susceptibility testing rather than conventional antimicrobial susceptibility testing in the treatment of Pseudomonas aeruginosa pulmonary infections in people with cystic fibrosis.

key_points.statement: Current evidence is insufficient to recommend choosing antibiotics based on biofilm antimicrobial susceptibility testing rather than conventional antimicrobial susceptibility testing in the treatment of Pseudomonas aeruginosa pulmonary infections in people with cystic fibrosis.

Biofilm susceptibility testing was not shown to be superior to conventional susceptibility testing regarding microbiological outcomes, specifically the change in sputum Pseudomonas aeruginosa density.
Biofilm susceptibility testing was not shown to be superior to conventional susceptibility testing in terms of lung function outcomes.
No difference was demonstrated between biofilm and conventional susceptibility testing regarding risk and time to subsequent exacerbation or quality of life measures.
The use of biofilm antimicrobial susceptibility testing was shown to be safe.

title: Inhaled mannitol for cystic fibrosis.
research_query: What is the efficacy and safety of inhaled dry powder mannitol compared to placebo, active inhaled comparators (e.g., hypertonic saline or dornase alfa), or no treatment in improving lung function, quality of life, and managing adverse events in individuals with cystic fibrosis?
overall_conclusion: There is moderate-quality evidence that mannitol improves some measures of lung function over six months compared to control, but low to very low-quality evidence suggests no difference in quality of life compared to control, and very low-quality evidence suggests no difference in lung function or quality of life when compared to dornase alfa alone or mannitol plus dornase alfa.

key_points.statement: There is moderate-quality evidence that treatment with mannitol over a six-month period is associated with an improvement in some measures of lung function in people with cystic fibrosis compared to control, while evidence for quality of life and comparisons with dornase alfa is of low to very low quality and suggests no difference.

In pooled large parallel studies, lung function (forced expiratory volume at one second) measured in mL and % predicted was significantly improved in the mannitol group compared to the control group (moderate-quality evidence).

There were no consistent differences in health-related quality of life domains between mannitol and control groups, except for burden of treatment, which was less for mannitol up to four months in two pooled studies (low to very low-quality evidence).

No statistically significant differences were found between mannitol and control groups regarding rates of adverse events, although common side effects in both groups included cough, haemoptysis, bronchospasm, pharyngolaryngeal pain, and post-tussive vomiting.
Study results are not applicable to the cystic fibrosis population as a whole because only participants who tolerated an initial test of mannitol were randomised.

title: Normal saline (0.9% sodium chloride) versus heparin intermittent flushing for the prevention of occlusion in long-term central venous catheters in infants and children.
research_query: What are the clinical effects of intermittent flushing with normal saline compared to heparin for preventing occlusion in long-term central venous catheters in infants and children?
overall_conclusion: There is not enough evidence to determine the effects of intermittent flushing with normal saline versus heparin to prevent occlusion in long-term central venous catheters in infants and children.

key_points.statement: There is not enough evidence to determine the effects of intermittent flushing with normal saline versus heparin to prevent occlusion in long-term central venous catheters in infants and children.
The effect of normal saline compared to heparin on CVC occlusion per 1000 catheter days is uncertain.
The effect of normal saline compared to heparin on CVC-associated blood stream infection is uncertain.
The effect of normal saline compared to heparin on the duration of catheter placement is unclear.
The certainty of evidence ranged from moderate to very low due to a lack of blinding, high heterogeneity and inconsistency between studies, and wide confidence intervals.

title: Transarterial (chemo)embolisation versus no intervention or placebo for liver metastases.
research_query: What are the benefits and harms of transarterial embolisation (TAE) or transarterial chemoembolisation (TACE) compared with no intervention or placebo in people with liver metastases?
overall_conclusion: Evidence is very uncertain about the effect of TAE or TACE versus no active therapeutic intervention on mortality for people with liver metastases, as the true effect may be substantially different.

key_points.statement: Evidence is very uncertain about the effect of TAE or TACE versus no active therapeutic intervention on mortality for people with liver metastases, as the true effect may be substantially different.
Very-low-certainty evidence found little or no difference in mortality between the TAE group and the no intervention group, and between the TACE group and the no intervention group.

Short-term, minor adverse events, including post-embolisation syndrome and local puncture site haematoma, were recorded in the TAE group, while the TACE group experienced short-term nausea with or without vomiting, wound infection, and deep vein thrombosis.
The trial did not measure failure to clear liver metastases, time to progression of liver metastases, tumour response measures, or health-related quality of life.

title: Cognitive training interventions for dementia and mild cognitive impairment in Parkinson's disease.
research_query: Does cognitive training improve cognitive function, activities of daily living, or quality of life in individuals with Parkinson's disease dementia (PDD) or mild cognitive impairment in Parkinson's disease (PD-MCI)?
overall_conclusion: There is no evidence that people with PD-MCI or PDD who receive cognitive training for four to eight weeks experience any important cognitive improvements at the end of training, though this is based on a small number of studies with imprecise results.

key_points.statement: There is no evidence that people with PD-MCI or PDD who receive cognitive training for four to eight weeks experience any important cognitive improvements at the end of training.
There was no evidence of differences between cognitive training and control groups in activities of daily living or quality of life.
There was no clear evidence that cognitive training improved global cognition, executive function, or visual processing.
Evidence favoured cognitive training for attention and verbal memory, although these effects were less certain in sensitivity analyses.
The certainty of evidence for all outcomes was considered low due to risk of bias in the included studies and imprecision of the results.

title: Different unfractionated heparin doses for preventing arterial thrombosis in children undergoing cardiac catheterization.
research_query: What are the effects of low-dose (< 100 units/kg) versus high-dose (≥ 100 units/kg) unfractionated heparin administered as an intravenous bolus during cardiac catheterization on the prevention of arterial thrombosis, bleeding complications, and other adverse events in children aged 0 to 18 years?
overall_conclusion: The authors are unable to determine the effects of different dosing regimens of unfractionated heparin for the prevention of vascular thrombosis during cardiac catheterization in children due to limitations of the current evidence, the small number of included studies, and lack of reported details in one study.

key_points.statement: The authors are unable to determine the effects of different dosing regimens of unfractionated heparin for the prevention of vascular thrombosis during cardiac catheterization in children due to limitations of the current evidence, the small number of included studies, and lack of reported details in one study.
The risk of arterial thrombotic events was compatible with benefits of either high or low unfractionated heparin dose regimens.
One study found no clear difference in the incidence of major or minor bleeding events between low-dose and high-dose unfractionated heparin arms.
There was a non-significant difference in the incidence of deep vein thrombosis when comparing high versus low doses of heparin.
The certainty of the evidence for key outcomes was downgraded to moderate due to imprecision and concerns about risk of bias.

title: Sound reduction management in the neonatal intensive care unit for preterm or very low birth weight infants.
research_query: What are the effects of sound reduction interventions, such as silicone earplugs, on growth, neurodevelopmental outcomes, short-term medical outcomes, sleep patterns, staff performance, and parental satisfaction in preterm or very low birth weight infants in neonatal intensive care units?
overall_conclusion: Based on the small sample size of a single trial, no recommendations for clinical practice can be made regarding the effectiveness of reducing sound levels that reach infants' ears in the NICU.

key_points.statement: Based on the small sample size of a single trial, no recommendations for clinical practice can be made regarding the effectiveness of reducing sound levels that reach infants' ears in the NICU.
There was no significant difference in weight at 34 weeks postmenstrual age between infants using silicone earplugs versus no earplugs.
There was no significant difference in weight at 18 to 22 months corrected age between infants using silicone earplugs versus no earplugs.
Silicone earplugs were associated with a significant difference in the Mental Developmental Index (Bayley II) at 18 to 22 months corrected age compared to no earplugs.
There was no significant difference in the Psychomotor Development Index (Bayley II) at 18 to 22 months corrected age between infants using silicone earplugs versus no earplugs.

title: Interventions for chronic pruritus of unknown origin.
research_query: What are the effects of interventions, including non-pharmacological, topical, and systemic pharmacological treatments, on chronic pruritus of unknown origin (CPUO) in adults and children?
overall_conclusion: There is a lack of evidence to address the review question, as most interventions of interest had no eligible studies and the only assessable intervention, serlopitant, provided only low-certainty evidence regarding pruritus intensity and very low-certainty evidence for other outcomes.

key_points.statement: There is a lack of evidence to address the review question, as most interventions of interest had no eligible studies and the only assessable intervention, serlopitant, provided only low-certainty evidence regarding pruritus intensity and very low-certainty evidence for other outcomes.
Low-certainty evidence suggests that serlopitant may reduce patient-reported pruritus intensity as measured by the visual analogue scale (VAS) compared to placebo.
There is very low-certainty evidence regarding the effects of serlopitant compared to placebo on adverse events, health-related quality of life (DLQI), and sleep disturbances (PSSQ-I).
The most commonly reported adverse events associated with the studied intervention were somnolence, diarrhoea, headache, and nasopharyngitis.
Certainty of evidence for all outcomes was downgraded due to imprecision and indirectness, as only 55% of participants in the available study had chronic pruritus of unknown origin (CPUO).

title: Blood transfusions for treating acute chest syndrome in people with sickle cell disease.
research_query: What is the effectiveness of blood transfusions, including simple and exchange transfusions, compared to standard care in treating acute chest syndrome in individuals with sickle cell disease?
overall_conclusion: There is currently no reliable evidence to support or refute the perceived benefits of blood transfusions as treatment options for acute chest syndrome in people with sickle cell disease.

key_points.statement: There is currently no reliable evidence to support or refute the perceived benefits of blood transfusions as treatment options for acute chest syndrome in people with sickle cell disease.
In one small trial, no participants who received a single transfusion of 7 to 13 mL/kg packed red blood cells developed acute chest syndrome, compared to 33% of participants in the standard care arm.
No data for any pre-defined outcomes were available in the eligible trial.
There is very limited information regarding potential harms associated with blood transfusions for treating acute chest syndrome.
